{{Quote|Fighters straight ahead!|Ric Olié|<ref name="tpm" />}}
'''Ric Olié''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] and [[Starship/Legends|starship]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] who served in the [[Royal Naboo Security Forces/Legends|Royal Naboo Security Forces]]. He was the commander of the [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps/Legends|Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps]], and the leader of [[Echo Flight]], [[Alpha Flight (Naboo)|Alpha Flight]] and [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Squadron]]. An expert pilot, he was qualified to fly any vessel that was a part of Naboo's fleet.

Olié's talents also landed him the job of the [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|queen's]] personal pilot, often flying the [[J-type 327 Nubian royal starship/Legends|Royal starship]] in the service of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]. Due to Naboo's pacifism, Olié's skills were rarely in use, although he saw military action during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]. He was also slightly superstitious, and thought of his [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-A6/Legends|R2-A6]] as a good-luck charm.

==Biography==
===Early life===
In his youth, Olié's enthusiastic flying earned him the nickname "Reckless Ric." He flew short flights for civilians in his [[Sandtek]] [[Skyflipper]] around the land surrounding his small [[City/Legends|village]]. One [[Standard day/Legends|day]], he crashed his Skyflipper into one of Naboo's many grassy hills, a disaster that would discourage most from the dangerous profession of flying. Olié, however, was far from discouraged. He built a new craft from the broken parts of the old ship and continued piloting.<ref name="negtc" /> Eventually, he tempered his reckless behavior after seeing too many pilots [[Death/Legends|die]] in crashes.<ref name="FF" />

===Early career===
[[File:Bravo1-TPM.png|thumb|left|200px|Olié in his [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]] with astromech droid [[R2-A6/Legends|R2-A6]]]]
After graduating from public school, Olié enrolled in the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector's]] academy, hoping to land a career as a home guard pilot. Because of his loyalty to Naboo, he refrained from joining the [[Carida Academy/Legends|Republic Defense Academy]], instead joining the [[Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps/Legends|Naboo Royal Space Fighter Corps]].<ref name="goi">''[[Galaxy of Intrigue]]''</ref> Because he was unique among Naboo's fighter pilots in that he had actually seen combat, Olié was promoted to captain and placed in command of Theed's main fighter squadron, Bravo. Although some of his peers scoffed at his service in the Chommell sector, claiming that the enemy [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] were prone to flying into one another, [[Ars Veruna/Legends|Ars Veruna]] held the utmost faith in his abilities, and as a result, Olié was one of the first pilots to field-test the [[N-1 starfighter/Legends|N-1 starfighter]].<ref name="Star Wars: Darth Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

In [[Time/Legends|time]], he became head of the Space Fighter Corps, which put him in charge of [[Echo Flight|Echo]] and [[Alpha Flight (Naboo)|Alpha]] Flights,<ref name="negtc" /> as well as [[Bravo Squadron/Legends|Bravo Squadron]]<ref name="ccg1">{{CCG|set=Coruscant Limited|cardname=Ric Olié}}</ref>&mdash;Naboo's entire starfighter navy.<ref name="negtc" /> Since Bravo Flight was the most prominent of the three, Olié's call sign was Bravo Leader.<ref name="negtc" /> In his role, he flew his personal N-1 starfighter, the control configuration of which he had modified.<ref name="ccg2">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=Bravo 1}}</ref> His only superior in the Royal Naboo Security Forces was [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]],<ref name="negtc" /> who had handpicked him for his position over the starfighter corps.<ref name="FF" />

Olié disliked paperwork, and would often leave administrative chores to his second-in-command, [[Essara Till/Legends|Essara Till]], who would willingly accept the extra responsibility.<ref name="tst">{{GamerCite|1|The Starfighter Trap}}</ref> Olié was able to recognize skilled volunteers, such as [[Porro Dolphe/Legends|Porro Dolphe]], and acknowledged their abilities.<ref name="ccg3">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=Officer Dolphe}}</ref> Most of the pilots in Olié's care, however, were simple barge drivers or transport pilots, with very little combat experience, leaving them, like the rest of the Security Forces, ill-prepared for the coming threat.<ref name="negtc" />

===Invasion of Naboo ([[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]])===
{{Quote|Shield generator's been hit!|Ric Olié|<ref name="tpm" />}}
The Space Fighter Corps was not given much chance to defend Naboo when the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] blockaded the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] as a protest against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] new trade route taxation. Instead, Olié, along with the rest of his pilots, were captured and arrested by Federation forces when they swept into [[Theed/Legends|Theed]]. Their queen was also arrested, and Naboo was subjugated swiftly by the forces of [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]]. However, they did not anticipate the intervention of two [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who rescued the queen, her entourage, Olié, and his pilots. Olié had no time to comprehend what was going on, as he was quickly ushered into the Queen's Royal Starship, and ordered to set a heading for [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="tpm" />

Escape did not come easily, as the Federation's blockade significantly challenged Olié. He was flying an unarmed transport against a fleet of heavily armed capital ships. Although he tried his best, the ship sustained heavy damage during the escape, and lost its shield generator. [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], one of the ship's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]], repaired the shields, which allowed Olié to pilot the ship through the blockade to safety.<ref name="tpm" />

[[File:OlieSkywalker-TPM.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Olié teaches Anakin Skywalker.]]
During the escape, the [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] suffered enough damage to prevent the ship from finishing the journey to Coruscant. Kenobi suggested that they land on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], a desert planet, and purchase the parts needed to make repairs. Qui-Gon Jinn, the queen (in disguise), the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]], [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], and R2 set out to look for the parts. After a few days, they returned with both the parts and a new member of the group&mdash;nine-year-old [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], an aspiring pilot. Olié took to the boy and offered him a few short lessons in starship piloting. When the queen's pleas to the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] to send aid to her besieged planet went unheeded, she decided to return and take matters into her own hands. Olié flew the group back to Naboo to confront their Trade Federation adversaries. Olié's skills, combined with a lessened Trade Federation space presence, allowed them to land on the planet with enough time for Amidala to contact the native Gungans to enlist their help.<ref name="tpm" />

===The battle of Naboo===
{{Quote|We didn't hit it!|Ric Olié|<ref name="tpm" />}}
[[File:RicOliePilot-SWE.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Olié during the space battle over Naboo]]
The queen had a plan&mdash;the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] would assemble and draw OOM-9's forces out of Theed, she and Panaka would then sneak into the city and capture the [[Viceroy of the Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation Viceroy]], [[Nute Gunray/Legends|Nute Gunray]], and Olié and his pilots would attempt to knock out the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class Droid Control Ship]]. Destroying the ship was the key to deactivating all droid units and saving the outmatched Gungans.<ref name="tpm" />

When the queen and the Jedi liberated Theed's hangar, Olié and his pilots sprang into action, clambering into their N-1 starfighters and setting out for the Droid Control Ship.<ref name="tpm" /> As soon as his craft was airborne, Olié transmitted rendezvous coordinates for the squadron, whence they would launch their attack against the command ship.<ref name="ccg4">{{CCG|set=Theed Palace Limited|cardname=It's On Automatic Pilot!}}</ref> The Federation launched [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture'' droid starfighters]] in attempt to counter the Naboo offensive, and destroyed many of the N-1 fighters. Only upon reaching the enemy ship did Olié realize that the [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shield]] was too strong, and that the battle seemed hopeless. Just when it seemed as though the Naboo fighters would fail in their mission, Anakin Skywalker flew inside the ship and destroyed it. Bravo Flight jubilantly returned to their liberated homeworld.<ref name="tpm" />

===Post invasion===
Following the Federation's defeat, Olié attended the [[Funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|funeral of Qui-Gon Jinn]], who died in the battle, before participating in the [[Freedom of Naboo/Legends|celebrations]] held in Theed.<ref name="tpm" /> In the [[Standard year/Legends|years]] following Naboo's bloodiest conflict, he would accrue further fame with Bravo Flight.<ref name="negtc" /> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], his one-time protégé, Anakin Skywalker, went on to become a skilled pilot.<ref name="anh">{{Film|IV}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Coruscant&hellip; the entire planet is one big city.|Ric Olié|<ref name="tpm" />}}
Olié was a vocally observant man, and had a reputation among his peers as the one most likely to point out the obvious.<ref name="tpm" /> He was considerably brash in his youth, and instead of learning from his mistakes, he found only encouragement in failure. He was also extremely proud of his homeworld, and did not hesitate to "advertise" the skills of Bravo Squadron in front of foreigners.<ref name="negtc" />

He was a naturally gifted pilot and adapted to Naboo's military system quite easily. He was reverent towards his queen and always respected her decisions.<ref name="tpm" /> However, he understood that Naboo was an imperfect world, and did not always agree that tradition was the safest thing for his planet's welfare.<ref name="tst" /> Olié was also superstitious, believing that his astromech droid, R2-A6, was a good-luck charm.<ref name="db">{{DB|character|ricolie|Olié, Ric}}</ref>

When in the company of foreign pilots, namely those who flew for the Republic, Olié was prone to being a bit of a show-off. He participated in many minor skirmishes with Chommell sector pirates and would often escort dignitaries to Coruscant and back. During such missions, he would attempt to demonstrate his considerable skills.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:RicOlie1.png|thumb|right|300px|This is a picture of Ric Olié.]]
Ric Olié first appeared as a supporting character in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], where he was portrayed by [[Ralph Brown]]. Olié was voiced by [[Jess Harnell]] in [[Star Wars: Starfighter (video game)|''Star Wars: Starfighter'']] and [[Clint Bajakian]] in ''[[Star Wars: Episode I: Battle for Naboo]]''.

Ric Olié is referred to by some fans as [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|Captain Obvious]] due to dialogue that simply states well-observed facts, such as "There's the blockade!," "That's it&hellip; Tatooine," and "We didn't hit it!"<ref name="cbr">{{WebCite|url=http://forums.comicbookresources.com/showthread.php?156451-Rick-Olney-Fibber-or-Mega-Giganta-Fibber/page64|text=Rick Olney--Fibber or Mega-Giganta-Fibber?|date=2006-12-30|nobackup=1}}</ref><ref name="jcf">{{JCFCite|url=threads/25422484|board=EU Community|thread=Ric Olie one-liners}}</ref><ref name="ama">{{Amazon|url=review/R3FDURPHJV0H42|text=Customer review of ''Star Wars: The New Essential Guide to Characters''}}</ref>
